# BAD-084 — functions.test.mjs's stack probe cannot tell a half-up stack from a live one

## Brief
Observed on this machine while verifying BAD-079 (a test-only change to a different file).

Evidence: podman ps: 9 supabase_*_bad-takes containers Up 7 hours (healthy); pgrep -fl 'supabase functions serve': no process; curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:54321/functions/v1/license -> 503. npm test on an otherwise-clean worktree: tests 1770, pass 1655, fail 114, skipped 1 — failure locations group as 111 in test/server/functions.test.mjs and 3 in test/server/account.test.mjs, zero elsewhere. The same tree with those two files excluded: tests 1649, pass 1648, fail 0, skipped 1 (the skip is a mobile/node_modules build test, not a pack test).

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, no children. The change is two files in test/server/ and no production code, but the judgment is real: what distinguishes a half-up stack from a live one, and what each skip reason should tell the reader to do about it. The half-up stack is live on this machine right now, so both branches are verifiable without tearing anything down.
